description: The Quasi-Zenith Satellite System, known as Michibiki, is Japan's regional satellite navigation system, which complements GPS over Japan and the Asia-Oceania region and offers centimetre-level augmentation services. Service began in November 2018 with four satellites and the system is being expanded to seven, after which at least four Michibiki satellites will always be above Japan and the system can provide positioning on its own. The official technical site's operational information and archive section publishes the current status of the constellation, NAQU notices (notice advisories to QZSS users, announcing outages, manoeuvres and anomalies), results of service performance evaluations against the published performance standards, public archive data from the system, and an application programming interface for automated access. Coverage: Japan and the Asia-Oceania service area, 2018 onward. Format and access: web pages, downloadable archives and an API, free; file formats and archive spans are described on linked pages that were not read. Caveats: much documentation is in Japanese; performance results are the operator's own evaluation. Simulation uses: service availability and outage records of a regional navigation system, reference context for GNSS dependence in Japan, and inputs for disruption scenarios. Related records: the QZSS Disaster and Crisis Report case covers its messaging service, and the Galileo performance reports are the European counterpart.
